title: A Fish That Learns to Cancel Its Own Pulse

scenes.tts: An electric fish senses the world with its own pulses. Why does every pulse not mask what it listens for?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Fish That Learns to Cancel Its Own Pulse. A mormyrid fish with field lines spreading from its tail. A faint signal from another fish is buried under a large pulse trace. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: An electric fish senses the world with its own pulses. Why does every pulse not mask what it listens for?

scenes.tts: Each pulse also stimulates its passive electroreceptors. These only listen, for weak fields from outside sources.
scenes.visual: Receptors along the body light up with each pulse. Label: passive electroreceptors.
scenes.narration: Each pulse also stimulates its passive electroreceptors. These only listen, for weak fields from outside sources.

scenes.tts: The command that fires the electric organ is also copied to the electrosensory lobe.
scenes.visual: A command neuron sends one line to the electric organ and a branch to a box labelled electrosensory lobe; receptor fibres run into the same box.
scenes.narration: The command that fires the electric organ is also copied to the electrosensory lobe.

scenes.tts: Bell found that the effect of that copy is not fixed. It changed to match the input from the receptors.
scenes.visual: The copy trace in the lobe reshapes itself to follow changes in the receptor input. Caption: Bell, 1981.
scenes.narration: Bell found that the effect of that copy is not fixed. It changed to match the input from the receptors.

scenes.tts: Now the key test. Paralyse the fish. The brain still issues the command, but the electric organ no longer fires.
scenes.visual: Label: neuromuscular blocker. The command line stays active; the electric organ is crossed out. No pulse trace.
scenes.narration: Now the key test. Paralyse the fish. The brain still issues the command, but the electric organ no longer fires.

scenes.tts: Pair each command with an artificial stimulus that mimics a pulse. Then switch the stimulus off.
scenes.visual: Each command tick is followed by an artificial stimulus trace with an upward bump. Then the stimulus trace disappears, leaving the command tick and a flat lobe trace.
scenes.narration: Pair each command with an artificial stimulus that mimics a pulse. Then switch the stimulus off.

scenes.tts: Predict. What does the command alone now do in the lobe?
scenes.visual: The flat lobe trace with a question mark. Text: Predict.
scenes.narration: Predict. What does the command alone now do in the lobe?

scenes.tts: It evokes a mirror of the paired input. Where the stimulus excited the cells, the command alone inhibits them.
scenes.visual: A dashed baseline labelled level before pairing. The lobe trace dips below that baseline exactly where the paired stimulus had an upward bump. A ghost of the old bump shows faintly above.
scenes.narration: It evokes a mirror of the paired input. Where the stimulus excited the cells, the command alone inhibits them.

scenes.tts: This mirror is called a negative image. Added to the real input, it cancels it.
scenes.visual: The bump and the dip add, and the sum draws as a flat line on the dashed baseline. Label: negative image.
scenes.narration: This mirror is called a negative image. Added to the real input, it cancels it.

scenes.tts: It was learned, because it followed whatever stimulus had been paired.
scenes.visual: A different paired stimulus shape appears, and a matching new mirror forms beneath it.
scenes.narration: It was learned, because it followed whatever stimulus had been paired.

scenes.tts: How does one command become a mirror with the right timing? Kennedy and colleagues recorded in awake, paralysed fish.
scenes.visual: A single command tick and a question: the right timing? Caption: Kennedy and colleagues, 2014.
scenes.narration: How does one command become a mirror with the right timing? Kennedy and colleagues recorded in awake, paralysed fish.

scenes.tts: Granule cells respond to the command at different delays. Unipolar brush cells add delayed responses.
scenes.visual: A fan of small cells under the command line, each with a bump at a different time. Later bumps labelled unipolar brush cells.
scenes.narration: Granule cells respond to the command at different delays. Unipolar brush cells add delayed responses.

scenes.tts: Together they form a temporal basis, a bank of signals each peaking at a different moment.
scenes.visual: Eight to ten bumps stacked along a time axis after the command, all feeding one medium ganglion cell. Label: temporal basis.
scenes.narration: Together they form a temporal basis, a bank of signals each peaking at a different moment.

scenes.tts: Two rules set their strengths. An input followed shortly by a broad spike in the cell's dendrites is weakened.
scenes.visual: Rule 1 card: input, then a broad dendritic teaching spike, synapse weakened (anti-Hebbian). The broad spike is drawn wide and labelled dendritic teaching spike; thin narrow output spikes beside it are labelled output spikes, no effect. A bump just before the broad spike shrinks.
scenes.narration: Two rules set their strengths. An input followed shortly by a broad spike in the cell's dendrites is weakened.

scenes.tts: And every active input is strengthened a little, whether or not the cell fires.
scenes.visual: Rule 2 card: every active input, a small boost. All bumps nudge upward slightly.
scenes.narration: And every active input is strengthened a little, whether or not the cell fires.

scenes.tts: On average, each active synapse weakens or strengthens according to the broad teaching spikes that follow it. With enough differently timed inputs, learning shrinks the predicted response.
scenes.visual: Label at top: simplified time-bin model, averaged learning. Repeated pulses: bumps that are often followed by broad dendritic teaching spikes (drawn wide) shrink, bumps rarely followed by them grow; thin narrow output spikes beside them are labelled no effect. The modulation of the cell's response around its baseline gets smaller with each repetition; no single target line.
scenes.narration: On average, each active synapse weakens or strengthens according to the broad teaching spikes that follow it. With enough differently timed inputs, learning shrinks the predicted response.

scenes.tts: So learning shrinks the response to the pulse. The command alone now dips where the pulse excited the cell.
scenes.visual: Top panel, zero-centred axis labelled change from pre-learning response: the learned change in the command response (purple) dips below zero where the pulse excited the cell; the pulse's effect (gold) rises above zero at the same moment; their sum draws as a line at zero, labelled zero residual modulation. Bottom panel, absolute response: pre-learning baseline (grey dashed) plus learned change plus pulse effect, 10 + (−6) + 6 = 10 in the middle bin, giving a flat trace labelled baseline response. Small text: all synapses stay excitatory.
scenes.narration: So learning shrinks the response to the pulse. The command alone now dips where the pulse excited the cell.

scenes.tts: A model built on these recordings learned to cancel the predicted input. The limit: a paralysed fish, plus a model.
scenes.visual: Scope card: paralysed fish plus a model; not a swimming fish.
scenes.narration: A model built on these recordings learned to cancel the predicted input. The limit: a paralysed fish, plus a model.

scenes.tts: Take this with you. Using a copy of the command, the circuit learns a timed negative image of the expected input.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: a command copy drives a learned, timed negative image of the expected input, reducing its central effect. Beneath, a flat residual trace around a labelled baseline.
scenes.narration: Take this with you. Using a copy of the command, the circuit learns a timed negative image of the expected input.
